subject: Sample Size of Site & Obs-level Covariates

messages.author: df2ff87426a98fc9
messages.subject: Sample Size of Site & Obs-level Covariates
parts:
Hello Group,

I have double-observer data that was collected during two survey occasions but not all sites were surveyed twice. I am trying to model the detection process in relation to site-level and observation-level covariates, but because of the missing data, p(site) and p(obs) models have different sample sizes and thus cannot be compared using AIC. Any suggestions on how to simultaneously examine the effects of these covariates would be much appreciated.

Cheers,
Dan

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: Sample Size of Site & Obs-level Covariates
parts:
If you standardize your covariates, you could set the missing values to zero which is essentially assigning them a mean value.  Since their response should be an NA, they do not contribute to the likelihood but the data structure is maintained.  This is not recommended for situations with many missing values and there are some implications of doing this, so I would look at section 11.6 in the MARK book for a better understanding:

http://www.phidot.org/software/mark/docs/book/

parts:
I do have a large number of missing values where surveys were intentionally missed, so I don't think that is a viable option.

I have attached a subset of the data to go along with the code below. As you can see, models with the different types of covariates have very different AIC values.

Thanks in advance for the help.

Cheers,
Dan


data<-read.csv("test.sample.size.csv")

library(unmarked)

# ------------> Set Up piFun and obsToY <------------ #
# piFun
depDoublePiFun <- function(p) {
    M <- nrow(p)
    pi <- matrix(NA, M, 2)
    pi[,1] <- p[,1]
    pi[,2] <- p[,2]*(1-p[,1])
    return(pi)
}

#obsToY
obsToY <- matrix(1, 2, 2)
numPrimary <- 2
obsToY <- kronecker(diag(numPrimary), obsToY)

# ------------> Set Up UMF <------------ #
y<-as.matrix(subset(data,select=c(count_S1_O1,count_S1_O2,count_S2_O1,
    count_S2_O2)))

siteCovs<-data.frame(sitecov=data$sitecov)

obsCovs<-list(obscov = as.matrix(subset(data,select=c(
    obscov_S1_O1,obscov_S1_O2,obscov_S2_O1,obscov_S2_O2))))

umf<-unmarkedFrameGMM(y=y, siteCovs=siteCovs, obsCovs=obsCovs,
    numPrimary=numPrimary, obsToY=obsToY, piFun="depDoublePiFun")
summary(umf)

# ------------> Fit Models <------------ #
m1 <- gmultmix(~1,~1,~1, data=umf, control=list(trace=TRUE))
m2 <- gmultmix(~1,~1,~obscov, data=umf, control=list(trace=TRUE))
m3  <- gmultmix(~1,~1,~sitecov, data=umf,control=list(trace=TRUE))

fms <- fitList(        "(.)" = m1,
                "(obscov)" = m2,
                "(sitecovs)" = m3)
(ms <- modSel(fms))
